message.content:

   • End Date: *The 7th of March* – Is that March 7 of this year (which has already passed) or March 7 next year (March 7 2027)?  

Once I have those details nailed down, I’ll check availability for an SUV picking up at **10:00 AM** on your chosen start date.

End date 2026-03-07? Wait that's earlier than today - maybe they mean 7th of next month? But user says "from today until the 7th of March". Today presumably May 18 2026, so future date March 7 2026 is past. Maybe they meant March 7 of this year? That also passed. Could be mis-specified. We might interpret as "today until March 7 of next year" i.e., 2027-03-07. Or ask clarification.

But guidelines: If ambiguous, clarify. So better ask clarifying question about intended dates. Also mention pickup time 10:00 AM. Let's respond asking for correct dates.
